sections.content:
Good , all things about consolidation

This course focuses on advanced financial accounting topics including intercorporate investments (with significant influence/control) and cross-border activities. Core contents cover business combinations, investor accounting for stock investments, consolidated financial statements (introduction, techniques, changes in ownership, indirect/mutual holdings), intercompany profit transactions (inventories, plant assets, bonds), subsidiary preferred stock & consolidated EPS, and foreign currency financial statements/transactions. It adheres to IFRS, emphasizing practical application via problem-solving, and integrates international dimensions, ethical responsibilities of accounting.

sections.teaching: Peter is a very good teacher in Acct department. He is very friendly and tried his best to help us understand the complicated consolidation accounting. He has some accent that you have to get used to it. In general I think you can understand 95% of lectures after attending 3-4 classes. He explains everything in detail and is open to any questions. You can feel free to ask questions during or after class. He also prints out assignments for us to work on.
sections.grading:
Assignment 10%
Midterm 40%
Final 50%

The assignments are easy, in general everyone gets a full mark. There will be ~4-5 assignments in total.

Midterm: mean = 67.12, sd = 19.68, me = 99, the full mark is 105.

Final: not released, non-cumulative

Remember both midterm and final DO NOT ALLOW CHEATSHEET.

Overall A+, very happy with it.
sections.workload: Very low to be honest. Only a few assignments that you can finish in ~10-15 mins if you attended and understand the lecture well. The thing is you have to make sure you know how to do the calculation and the format of different consolidations before the exams are they are not open books and no cheatsheet is allowed. I will recommend you spend some time working on the exercise provided by Peter. You will find it very useful.

sections.content: Consolidation of financial statements; starts from very basic situations (recognizing goodwill whilst disolving subsidiary) to adjusting inter-company transactions. First 4 chapters are very important, so make sure you understand fully how the figures are calculated. Peter only teaches the basic method on how to arrive on those figures, but the textbook will elaborate on other methods.
sections.teaching: Because consolidation is very complicated, Peter encourages us to attend every lecture. He knows the concepts and methodologies well, but his English is not so good, and one can easily doze off, especially in the afternoon. He follows the PPT strictly, but he will happily answer any questions you raise throughout class. After a lot of lecturing, he will give out handouts for us to practice in-class. But his time management is not so good, so sometimes he rushes in the end.
sections.grading:
15% is awarded based on the group exercises. Peter mentioned that he would like us to finish them in-class, but in the end, he would let us take the exercises home and hand them in next class.
40% is for the mid-term, and it covered the first 5 chapters. Closed book, but can bring cheat sheet.
45% is for the final, non-cumulative. But a lot of the content after the midterm is built upon the content of previous sessions. Open-book, so label your book and notes carefully to quickly find the entries needed. Time is tight for both exams. Make sure you print the handouts and solutions too because the finals will feature the exact questions.
Peter won't fail anyone, but accounting courses are extremely competitive in UST so try your best.
sections.workload: Practice makes perfect; this is exceptionally true for accounting courses. Finish his recommended exercises at the end of the textbook and you'll be fine.

sections.content: Compulsory course for ACCT major. Covers more advanced financial accounting concepts such as consolidated financial statements and different kinds of journal entries required (for consolidated assets, liabilities, equity) when mergers and acquisitions happen. Some small parts like EPS, indirect and mutual holdings will also be discussed.
sections.teaching: Peter is a very nice professor. He always tries his best to answer the questions and explain the concepts. However, as this was the very first time he taught the course, he was not very familiar with the course materials and sometimes made some mistakes in the class. He may also speed up when he found that he did not have enough time to teach (and then cannot explain the concepts clearly...). Nevertheless, Peter has shown his passion in teaching and worked hard to explain those complex entries and concepts. :)
sections.grading:
Grading should be quite good, as the mean of ACCT compulsory course is around B.

Grading Scheme:
Group Exercises: 15%
Midterm: 40%
Final: 45%
sections.workload:
Workload is not heavy as there is no project/presentation. Almost every lesson the prof. gives a 1-2 pages group exercise and you can use it to revise what you have learnt, and won't cost you much time to finish.

The midterm is closed-book exam but the final one is open-book. The level of difficulty is moderate and as long as you have tried the questions in the textbook, you shall be fine. All in all, accounting is a subject which requires lots of practice and understanding and practice makes perfect.
